title: Page and store access matrix

title: Store fan-in and fan-out
caption: silver_enriched_tracks is the busiest store (3 flows in, 2 out); 31 of 48 stores sit on a numbered flow.
source: flows[] (from, to, channel, state), stores[], signals[] for the contract
method: In = flows whose target is the store, out = flows whose source is the store; main contract = the signal named by the store's most frequent flow channel.

title: Timing constants on a log axis
caption: 105 timing constants span 100 ms to 365 d; reference lines mark Heartbeat stale (sn-be-t-heartbeat-stale), Job lease (sn-be-t-lease-default), Job stall (sn-fe-t-stall), Token lifetime (ml-t-tidal-user-default).
source: timings[].value_ms, timings[].kind, timings[].state
method: Each constant is one dot on a log10 axis, one lane per kind (kinds ordered by median value); coincident dots stack. Reference lines are the timings matched by name: heartbeat staleness, default job lease, job stall threshold and default token lifetime.

title: Polling load by target store (Estimate)
caption: Estimate: the heaviest polling target is via Melbourne crate (3 stores), 1,800 requests per hour; queued work adds no polling.
source: timings[] (kind poll|schedule, value_ms, where), signals[] and flows[] to resolve the store
method: Estimate: requests per hour = 3,600,000 / value_ms per poll or schedule timing, summed by target store; the target is the timing's own store, else the single store linked to its component by signals or flows, else the component is named with its store count. Assumes every tick makes one request.

title: Sizes against limits
caption: None of the 11 measured limits is within 10 % of its limit; the one with least headroom is ARIA parse sanity floor at 125 % of its floor.
source: limits[] with current (value, unit, current)
method: Bullet chart: current / limit. Text currents take their first number; a file map takes its largest file (the limit is per file), bytes to MB at 1,048,576. Floors (name says floor or minimum) are near when under 110 %, others when at or over 90 %.
